title: How do we expand three squares that have a minus sign?
description: The square of eigh minus b is used for b minus six, for negative two eigh plus three, and for seven y minus three over four z. Keeko doubts that the square of negative two eigh keeps its minus sign.
teaching_notes: One idea: in the square of eigh minus b, the middle term takes the minus sign and the last term stays plus. Watch for students who write the square of a negative term with a minus sign.

video_script.why: The child has expanded the square of a sum and cut a smaller square from a bigger one. Here the middle term takes a minus sign.
video_script.substitution: Put the two terms in the pattern with the minus sign in the middle, square each term, and tidy the middle term.
video_script.anchor: three squares, each with a minus sign inside
video_script.wrong_answer: the square of negative two eigh is minus four eigh squared
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko squares negative two eigh and keeps the minus sign, getting minus four eigh squared. A negative times a negative is positive, so the square must be plus four eigh squared.
video_script.payoff_line: The middle term carries the minus sign

final_answer.spoken: b squared, minus twelve b, plus thirty six; four eigh squared, minus twelve eigh, plus nine; forty nine y squared, minus twenty one y over two z, plus nine over sixteen z squared

video_script.fraction_reading: three over four z means three on top and four z below
maths_rules: (−2a)² = (−2a) × (−2a) = 4a², since a negative times a negative is positive
video_script.design: One idea: the square of eigh minus b, with the middle term taking the minus sign. Uses the square of a sum. Wrong idea: the square of a negative term keeps its minus sign. The three workings stay on the board through the doubt.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>The square of eigh minus b is eigh squared, minus two eigh b, plus b squared.

marks.put: b and 6 are put in the pattern

narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Step one, the first expression has the terms b and six.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice b times six is twelve b, and it takes the minus sign.
<bookmark mark='last'/>Six squared is thirty six, so the result is b squared, minus twelve b, plus thirty six.

marks.mid: 2 × 3 × 2a = 12a is written with a minus sign before it
marks.sq2: (2a)² = 4a² is written, and 9 − 12a + 4a² is read off

beats.colours: each piece in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Step two, put the positive term first, which gives three minus two eigh, squared.
<bookmark mark='sq1'/>Three squared is nine.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice three times two eigh is twelve eigh, with the minus sign.
<bookmark mark='sq2'/>Two eigh, squared, is four eigh squared.
That gives nine, minus twelve eigh, plus four eigh squared.

marks.put: 7y and 3/(4z) are put in the pattern
marks.mid: 2 × 7y × 3/(4z) = 42y/(4z) is written with a minus sign before it

beats.colours: each piece in its own colour
narration: <bookmark mark='put'/>Step three, the terms are seven y and three over four z.
<bookmark mark='sq1'/>Seven y, squared, is forty nine y squared.
<bookmark mark='mid'/>Twice seven y times three over four z is forty two y over four z.
<bookmark mark='red'/>That reduces to twenty one y over two z, with the minus sign.
<bookmark mark='sq2'/>Three over four z, squared, is nine over sixteen z squared.

marks.pay: the words the middle term carries the minus sign appear

narration: <bookmark mark='pay'/>The middle term carries the minus sign.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>The first is b squared, minus twelve b, plus thirty six.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>The second is four eigh squared, minus twelve eigh, plus nine.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>The third has forty nine y squared, minus twenty one y over two z.
<bookmark mark='a4'/>Its last piece is nine over sixteen z squared.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the square of negative two eigh is minus four eigh squared.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it with eigh as one. Negative two times negative two is positive four.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>A negative times a negative is positive, so the square cannot keep the minus sign.
